items.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: There’s a new singer, a young singer, I guess he’s in the pop idiom, Maxwell I think his name is, I like some of the ballads he’s doing.

ctx.x: Do you have any feelings about popular music these days?

I don’t listen to much of it. I don’t. You know I just don’t listen to it much. The melodies that I’ve grown up with, where have they gone? They were so beautiful. I liked some of Burt Bacharach’s things that he did with Dionne Warwick. There’s a new singer, a young singer, I guess he’s in the pop idiom, Maxwell I think his name is, I like some of the © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

ballads he’s doing. But some of the things I hear — and these people are nominated for Grammys and you know, nominated for this award and that award, and making bookoos of money, I just wonder, where is the talent? Where is the talent? I don’t hear it and I don’t feel it. You know so most of the times I’m listening to either the jazz station or I listen to the talk stations a lot which are non-musical.
